cost_model.label: DESIGN ESTIMATE -- no completion runs were performed
cost_model.formula: cost(tau) = N_anchor(tau) x [10, 30] desktop-minutes per anchor (A35 measured steady-state re-run of one critical point with the repaired pipeline, final_report.md cost table)
cost_model.anchor: anchor = spine type + one 3-degree tilt bin per tilt class + one geometric branch per link + one x-cell (width = cell_width) per square; N_anchor is the ARC-CONSISTENT count, an upper bound
cost_model.unpriced: the anchor pins NO transverse coordinate: y_i is free over [h(phi_i), s0 - h(phi_i)] for every spine square, and the 11 - k rattlers are entirely unpinned.  A35 measured the semantic cliff R* = (min non-contact gap)/L_pair = 0.024875/4.2426 = 0.00586: below that radius a cell keeps its contact semantics, above it the contact set changes and the per-anchor cost model does not transfer.  A free y-interval of length ~2.9 is ~490 R*-cells per square, so the honest cost is the table below TIMES an unpriced factor of order 490^k x (rattler factor) unless a completion argument discharges the transverse directions analytically.

gaps.text: The lambda0 = 0 branch (global compression self-stress, structure_lemmas L6) is NOT covered: L6 produces a wall-to-wall H-component only when lambda0 > 0.  Same named residual as A31.

SPINE = a SHORTEST wall-to-wall H-path.  L6 guarantees a spanning H-COMPONENT, and every spanning component contains at least one shortest wall-to-wall path, so the census is complete for the existence question.  It is NOT a census of all spanning chains: a longer non-shortest chain in the same component carries a type that may not appear here.  Any downstream completion argument must be phrased as "the shortest spine has type tau", not "every chain has type tau".

Spine squares are required DISTINCT and consecutive pairs must have an ACTIVE LOADED contact.  Contacts of a spine square to squares OFF the spine are not modelled: dx intervals use only the on-spine link, so the census cannot see a configuration killed by an off-spine neighbour.  This is a relaxation (it can only over-accept).

x-cell discretisation.  The layered DP tests ARC (pairwise) consistency between consecutive cells, not full chain consistency, so both survival and N_anchor are over-approximations.  Exact chain interval propagation IS run separately as the C0/C1 stage (c0_alive), and the composed C2 verdict is the conjunction of the two.
The C-end tilt window is taken as the closed bin [0, 3] deg for bin 0, which includes phi = 0; a wall-corner end actually needs phi in (0,90).  Outward, hence sound (over-accepting).
Containment uses the widest box [h_lo(bin), s - h_lo(bin)] rather than the realisation-dependent [h(phi), s - h(phi)].  Outward, sound.

C3 (W1 tight-variety) and C4 (A25 wastage) are evaluated over windows whose y-extent is the FULL admissible range, because a spine pins no transverse coordinate.  Both are therefore structurally inert here; the numbers are reported, not assumed.

C4 uses sum-of-per-square-minima as the certified wastage FLOOR.  min(sum) >= sum(min), so the reported floor under-states the true floor: conservative for a kill test, and it is also why the floor is 0 wherever any reachable window is uncovered by the atlas.

A37 valley canaries run at their OWN s (> s-hat).  The A33/A39 guard field and the A25 atlas exist only at s0 = 3.877084, so C3 and C4 are reported as null for those entries; their C0-C2 checks are complete.

A37 family 27 (VALLEY-MARGINAL) has no cert file under results/certs/, so its coordinates come from atlas_final.json canonical_sig, which is rounded to 6 decimals.  Contact extraction tolerance 1e-6 is at that scale; its canary verdict is therefore weaker evidence than the others.

Support graph vs active-contact graph: the canaries extract the ACTIVE-CONTACT graph G.  For Trump A22 certified strict complementarity, so H = G and the extracted paths are genuine spines.  For the A37 valleys no such certificate exists, so their chains are G-paths that CONTAIN the H-paths; using them can only make the canary harder to pass, never easier.

Floats with outward rounding throughout: math.nextafter on every arithmetic step and an absolute slop of 1e-9 on every cos/sin/tan evaluation (libm error < 1e-15 on the ranges used).  No kill depends on a difference smaller than 1e-9.
k <= 11 is the trivial cap.  k = 8..11 are counted under C0-C2 only and at the coarser 1/8 cell width, so those counts are upper bounds.

Survivor LISTS for k = 6 and k = 7 (2074 and 8249 entries) are written to results/h2/survivors_k6.txt and survivors_k7.txt, one line per type with its structure description; the JSON carries the full per-type records only for k <= 5 plus, for k = 6,7, the 15 largest and 15 smallest by N_anchor and the aggregate C3/C4/C5/C6 columns (which are constant: 0, 0, false, 0).
The canary enumerates all shortest wall-to-wall paths with a cap of 20000 per axis; no configuration came close (max 16).  Trump has 14 x-axis + 16 y-axis chains, the A37 entries 8-16 each.

A37 family 14 -- the cert file fam14_3S.json carries a z_center whose s equals family 13s (3.897230787), not its own atlas s_min 3.897462: the A37 atlas records {13,14} as a stratum MERGE, so the two share a configuration.  The canary therefore ran family 14 on the merged configuration at s = 3.897231; its bounding box was verified to be exactly [0, s]^2.

findings: HEADLINE. The shortest-spine census at s0 = 969271/250000 = 3.877084 survives the full C0-C4 stack with k=3: 10/36, k=4: 132/136, k=5: 523/528, k=6: 2074/2080, k=7: 8249/8256 (canonical types, up to reversal), and the C0-C2 DP count continues k=8: 32888/32896, k=9: 131319/131328, k=10: 524790/524800, k=11: 2098165/2098176.  The spine constraint alone does NOT close the structure space: it is a 72% cut at k = 3 and a <0.4% cut at every k >= 4.

WHERE IT BITES. k = 3: 36 raw -> 18 after C0 (span: 2 links carry at most 2 sqrt2 = 2.828427 < s0 - 1 = 2.877084, so EVERY F-F type dies, and most F-C types die too) -> 14 after C1 -> 10 after C2.  All 10 k = 3 survivors are C-C (both ends wall-CORNER, i.e. both end squares tilted); no k = 3 spine can have a wall-flush end.  k = 3 is also the ONLY length at which the census forces a nontrivial tilt window: C-FL.FL-C forces its single tilt class into [18, 72] deg and the four C-FL.X-C types force their flush class into [12, 78] deg.  At every k >= 4 every non-zero class window is the full [0, 90].

FROM k = 4 UP the ONLY kills are C1 (tilt coupling), and there are exactly k of them per length: one type F-FL^(k-1)-C (the whole path is one flush class pinned to phi = 0 by the left wall, so the right end cannot be a wall CORNER) and k-1 types F-FL^a.CE.FL^b-F (a single CE link between the two wall-flush zero classes, which A31 level1 forbids).  C0 kills NOTHING for k >= 4: with k-1 >= 3 links of reach sqrt2 the span identity is slack by more than a full link.

C1 REDUCTION (new, worth recording). On a PATH the tilt-class digraph is itself a path (a cycle only when both ends are wall-flush), and an acyclic orientation with the zero class as a source always exists.  So A31 level1 feasibility collapses to exactly two local rules: no CE link between two wall-flush zero classes, and no wall-corner end inside a zero class.  Everything else in the tilt subsystem is free.

C3 (W1 tight-variety) is INERT: 0 kills at every k, and the maximum certified min-coverage over any survivor window is 0.000000 against the threshold 1 + eta = 8768483/6250000 = 1.402957280 (A39 resealed field, standalone PASS, 1468 atoms, D4-closed).  Reason: a spine pins no transverse coordinate, so every square window spans y in [h, s0 - h] and mlow_box over such a box is essentially 0.

C4 (A25 interface wastage, single atlas at s0) is INERT: 0 kills, and the certified wastage FLOOR is exactly 0 for every survivor at every k, because every reachable window reaches deep-interior atlas cells whose dead area is genuinely 0.  Budget B0 = s0^2 - 11 = 4.031780343 was never approached.

C5 (A21 THM3 forcing) is FALSE for every survivor at every k and C6 (N8 band count) is identically 0 -- both computed, not assumed.  C6 is provably inert here: with y free the certified wall-clearance lower bound of every spine square is <= 0.

CANARY 1 (Trump at s0): the active-contact graph reproduces the known 14 square-square contacts; there are 30 shortest wall-to-wall chains (14 on the x axis at k = 4, 16 on the y axis at k = 5).  ALL 30 pass every realized-point check (C0 end identities, span identity, dx in the certified branch union, |delta| in [1, sqrt2], C1, the realized anchor being admitted by the C2 DP, the capacity lemma, C3 and C4) AND all 30 realized types are census survivors at s0.  0 failures.

TILTED STRIP. The 5 tilted squares of Trump are pairwise FLUSH and form a 5-chain 6-9-7-8-10 in the contact graph, but that chain is NOT wall-to-wall on a single axis (square 6 touches only the top wall, square 10 only the right wall).  The strip appears in the census as the y-axis spine F-CEab.FL.FL.FL-C at k = 5 -- 1 upright + 4 tilted, flush core FL.FL.FL -- which occurs in 4 of the 16 y-axis chains and survives.  That is the maximal-tilt spine Trump possesses.

CANARY 2 (A37 attractors): all 12 RIGID/VALLEY/VALLEY-MARGINAL entries PASS at their own s -- 0(RIGID, s=3.877084, 30 chains), 1(VALLEY, s=3.885618, 9 chains), 2(VALLEY, s=3.885618, 8 chains), 6(VALLEY, s=3.886746, 12 chains), 13(VALLEY, s=3.897231, 12 chains), 14(VALLEY, s=3.897231, 12 chains), 27(VALLEY-MARGINAL, s=3.925149, 16 chains), 31(VALLEY, s=3.936964, 16 chains), A37-NEW-0(VALLEY, s=3.902674, 12 chains), A37-NEW-1(VALLEY-MARGINAL, s=3.912232, 8 chains), A37-NEW-2(VALLEY, s=3.924402, 12 chains), A37-NEW-3(VALLEY, s=3.925470, 16 chains) -- 163 chains in total, 0 failures.  Separately (INFORMATION, not a canary): every one of those realized types ALSO survives the census at s0, i.e. none of the valley structures is excluded by the spine stack at s-hat.

INDEPENDENT KILL AUDIT: a second implementation (no bins, no cells, no outward rounding, direct tilt grid) re-searched all 48 killed types at k = 3..7 for a witness and found NONE.  The kills are not artefacts of the 3-degree binning or the x-cell relaxation.

COST (DESIGN ESTIMATE, no completion runs). Per-survivor anchor counts span 10^2.7 at k = 3 up to 10^18.2 at k = 7; the total over all k = 3..7 survivors is 10^20.3 anchors, i.e. 1.295e+18-3.886e+18 desktop-days at A35's measured 10-30 desktop-minutes per anchor.  And that is BEFORE the unpriced transverse dimension: an anchor pins no y_i at all and no rattler, and A35's semantic cliff R* = 0.00586 means a free y-interval of length ~2.88 is ~490 semantic cells per spine square.  The per-spine completion programme is not affordable as posed.

COMPOSE VERDICT for the A43 lead: H2 answers "large", not "small".  The constraint that failed to bite is the pair (C3, C4) -- both are PLACEMENT filters and a spine type is a PROJECTION that forgets y.  To make the spine census bite, the next lever must either (a) pin the transverse coordinate (e.g. carry a second, y-axis spine simultaneously -- L7 gives both axes their wall contacts whenever both bind), or (b) constrain the OFF-spine neighbours, since gap G3 shows the census currently models only the on-spine links.

kill_audit.method: independent second implementation (code/h2/audit_kills.py): plain float, no tilt bins, no x-cells, no outward rounding; direct grid over every tilt class plus every discrete branch label, with the continuous slide parameters handled exactly.  A witness would mean a census kill is UNSOUND.
